## F22.budget-caps — Budgets and caps

Definition: Spend or token limits a user or admin can set.
- claude-code [partial, verified] --max-budget-usd caps API spend before stopping, and spend from subagents counts toward the cap. The SDK max_budget_usd and maxBudgetUsd options stop the query when the client-side cost estimate reaches a USD value, and options can also limit turns, cost and reasoning depth. | limit: --max-budget-usd is print mode only. The SDK option counts only the call's own spend; totals restored from a resumed session don't count. | ev: E-claude-code-07067, E-claude-code-00537, E-claude-code-00975, E-claude-code-00174
- codex-cli [partial, verified] Admins can configure workspace defaults, group defaults, and user overrides for credit and usage controls. ## F22.rate-limits — Rate-limit behaviour

Definition: Plan limits, windows and what happens at the limit.
- claude-code [supported, unverified] When a claude.ai usage limit blocks a request, /rate-limit-options shows ways to keep working, including waiting to continue automatically when the limit resets and adding usage credits. Project usage counts against the same plan limits as other sessions. If the usage request fails, /usage shows the last usage bars it loaded within the past 60 minutes. | ev: E-claude-code-07290, E-claude-code-06940, E-claude-code-07441
- codex-cli [supported, verified] ChatGPT uses the same pricing, credits, and usage limits as Codex. Exhausted limits can pause access to eligible features. Codex rate-limit windows gate memory generation: a minimum remaining percentage is required before it starts (defaults to 25, clamped to 0-100). | ev: E-codex-cli-03615, E-codex-cli-02012, E-codex-cli-00620
- copilot-cli [partial, verified] Rate limits control how many requests a user or application can make in a given time period. Included AI credits do not carry over; the allowance resets at 00:00:00 UTC on the first day of each calendar month. Rate limits are temporary; waiting a short period and retrying often resolves them. A setting, when true, switches to auto mode and retries on eligible rate limit errors. | limit: The automatic switch to auto mode does not apply to global rate limits or BYOK providers. | ev: E-copilot-cli-02005, E-copilot-cli-01996, E-copilot-cli-02007, E-copilot-cli-01218
- copilot-vscode [supported, unverified] A temporary rate limit can occur even when the monthly AI credits allowance is not exhausted; wait a few minutes and retry. The inline suggestions and AI credits allowances reset every month; reaching only one does not block the other. The Copilot status dashboard in the Status Bar shows whether an allowance has been reached. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01803, E-copilot-vscode-00329, E-copilot-vscode-01821
- cursor [supported, unverified] At the usage limit you'll see a notification in the editor and can enable on-demand usage (pay-as-you-go) or upgrade to a higher plan. Balance and Intelligence use your usage limits faster than Cost. One endpoint is rate limited to 300 requests per minute and 6000 per hour. Back off using exponential delay (the SDK reports `isRetryable: true` for transient cases). | ev: E-cursor-04414, E-cursor-02802, E-cursor-00416, E-cursor-03858
- gemini-cli [supported, verified] For Log in with Google (Gemini Code Assist for individuals), the listed limit is 1000 maximum model requests / user / day. When rate-limited, the CLI automatically switches to the "flash" model. It tells you when you reach your Gemini 3 Pro daily usage limit. A 429 Resource exhausted error indicates the API request limit was exceeded. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00947, E-gemini-cli-00374, E-gemini-cli-00444, E-gemini-cli-02074
- grok-build [undocumented, verified] swept for: rate[- ]limit; \bquota; limit(s)? (reset|window); throttl; \b429\b; hits 4, reviewed 4; positive control `grok`: 349 hits
- grok-bot [supported, unverified] Paid Grok Bot access includes Weekly usage, which resets weekly. When it runs out, extra usage can continue as On-demand usage if on-demand is enabled. ## F22.telemetry-otel — Telemetry and OpenTelemetry

Definition: Metrics and traces the harness emits.
- claude-code [supported, unverified] OpenTelemetry export sends metrics from each developer's machine to your own observability stack, with per-user token counts, costs and tool activity. With CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1 set, each step of the agent loop becomes a trace span. The prompt_id field matches the prompt.id attribute on OpenTelemetry events. | ev: E-claude-code-07469, E-claude-code-00425, E-claude-code-01230
- codex-cli [partial, verified] OTel log export tracks Codex runs (API requests, SSE/events, prompts, tool approvals/results); it is disabled by default and opt-in via [otel]. Emitted events include user prompts (redacted by default) and tool approval decisions. - copilot-vscode [supported, unverified] Copilot Chat emits three types of OpenTelemetry signals: traces, metrics, and events. ## F22.logs-debug — Logs and debug output

Definition: Log files and debug switches.
- claude-code [supported, unverified] Per-session debug logs are written to debug/ while debug logging is on, started with --debug or /debug; the log is at ~/.claude/debug/‹session-id›.txt. claude logs ‹id› prints the session's recent output. The SDK debug option enables debug mode for the Claude Code process. | ev: E-claude-code-06849, E-claude-code-06308, E-claude-code-01782, E-claude-code-00958
- codex-cli [supported, verified] log_dir overrides where Codex writes local log files (default $CODEX_HOME/log); setting it explicitly also enables the opt-in plaintext TUI log, codex-tui.log. RUST_LOG controls Rust log filtering and verbosity; codex exec defaults to error output unless set more verbose. - copilot-vscode [supported, verified] Agent Debug Logs include Discovery events that show whether a customization was loaded, skipped, or rejected.
